title: Program Translation
definition: Program translation is the implementation-dependent transformation or interpretation that connects source representation to executable behavior.
purpose: Explain why processors do not directly execute arbitrary high-level source syntax and why compiler, interpreter, and JIT paths differ.
history: Assemblers, compilers, interpreters, virtual machines, and JIT systems evolved as different ways to bridge language abstraction and execution.
mental_model: Translation is a pipeline of representations, not necessarily one permanent source-to-binary step.
analogy: A translator can prepare a document before a meeting or interpret during it; the analogy fails because language tools must preserve formal semantics rather than human intent.
common_mistakes: Claiming all languages are either purely compiled or purely interpreted
Treating machine code as portable across every target
industry_notes: Production toolchains commonly combine parsing, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, linking, and runtime services.
ai_notes: AI explanations often collapse hybrid pipelines; verify claims against the exact implementation and version.
interview_notes: Evaluate whether the candidate can compare AOT, interpretation, and JIT without false binaries.
exercise_candidates: Draw two valid translation paths and state their limits
lab_candidates: Inspect an implementation's intermediate or emitted representation without teaching compiler construction
project_candidates: Document the execution path selected for the instruction simulator
